Hi there dear colleagues,
After lunch, the desk supervisor mentioned a few words on animal welfare

Please keep our handling notes crisp and practical so the cabin team can follow them without delay. When a traveler checks in with a pet, confirm the carrier condition, the feeding plan, and any comfort items that are allowed on board. If the traveler raises a concern about a lost crate, <<FACT F118>> and then guide them to the correct follow-up channel. Use calm language, stay brief, and make sure the traveler leaves with clear next steps.

For any report of cabin overheating, collect the basic service details, note the pet's behavior, and pass the case onward without adding extra commentary. <<FACT F111>> Keep your wording factual and supportive, since the goal is to protect the animal and keep the process smooth for operations. If a traveler seems unsettled, remind them that the crew is tracking conditions closely and that the desk will continue to coordinate the handoff. Be careful not to promise anything beyond what the service team can verify.

Please also remember that our companion animal guidance should stay consistent across the desk, the gate, and the cabin team. If Teddy or any other pet is mentioned in a handoff note, use the same wording that appears in the booking record and avoid casual guesses. Clear records make it easier for us to respond quickly, support the traveler, and keep the animal comfortable throughout the journey. Thanks for keeping the standard high and the communication steady.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
